text:
Zach Werenski won the Norris last season, and the start in Columbus has been fine without being that. Fourteen points in 16 games, 28 minutes a night, two goals on 49 shots.

The luck cuts both ways. Columbus has scored 6.4 more goals than expected with him on the ice, which is padding his points, and his own shooting (4%) is below his usual. Over his last ten he's at nine points on 9.8 expected, about even. The Blue Jackets are roughly even in chances at five on five with him on, which is the real gap from last season.

Last season's version is still the baseline. Evolving-Hockey had him fourth of 215 defensemen in wins above replacement, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 99th percentile for chances from the slot with 70% of his exits keeping possession. Our range: 68 to 96 points.
